Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · School & learning

section noun

of a law or a text

also sections, clause, article of a law, passage, chapter, chapters

classical

Cic. Att. 3.15.6: quoddam caput lēgis
Plin. Ep. 10.114.3
Traupman 273 (a clause in a law or a treaty)
Levi–Bini p. 7
Traupman 26, 28: caput quārtum, chapter four
M-O s.v. parts: chapter (division of book)

caput, capitis n.

noun, third declension

a section or head of a law or a writing; a chapter

Lewis & Short: “in writings, a division, section, paragraph, chapter”; ā prīmō capite lēgis usque ad extrēmum (Cic. Agr. 2.15).

Other words

  • locus, locī m. — a passage of a book

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 1.7: locōs quōsdam trānsferam (Lewis & Short)

    In this sense the plural is locī, not loca (Lewis & Short).

  • articulus, articulī m. — a clause; the article of a treaty

    noun, second declension · also used · post-classical · Dig. 36.1.27 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. article, clause; Levi–Bini p. 7

    The jurists’ word for a short clause; the articles of treaties and concordats in later Latin (Morgan–Owens).

Examples

  • Capita lēgis hīs litterīs subjēcī.

    I have appended the sections of the law to this letter.Plin. Ep. 10.114.3

  • at tūte scrīpsistī ad mē quoddam caput lēgis Clōdium in cūriae poste fīxisse, nē referrī nēve dīcī licēret

    but you wrote to me yourself that Clodius had nailed a section of the law to the doorpost of the senate house, forbidding the matter to be raised or spoken ofCic. Att. 3.15.6

See also part, page, book, article.

SourcesLewis & Short: caput · Lewis & Short: locus · Lewis & Short: articulus
